findings.note: Dead assertion: the nil-free-JSON check in TestFoldHappyPath can never fire. The snapshot always serializes PrevUnfixed as "prev_unfixed":null (types.go:225 has no omitempty, and line 192 of the same test asserts PrevUnfixed is nil on the happy path), so strings.Contains(js, `"prev_unfixed":null`) is always true and the negated second conjunct forces the condition to false unconditionally. I confirmed this by folding happyLog() and counting nulls in the canonical encoding: exactly one, prev_unfixed. The intent is 'no nulls other than prev_unfixed'; the code implements 'no nulls unless prev_unfixed is null'. The follow-up loop only pins lineage, goldens, warnings and vars, so a regression that let findings, confirmed, all_found, status, nodes_run, node_outputs, applied or allowed_cmds serialize as null would pass this test silently -- precisely the nil-free-container invariant this package exists to hold. Fix: strip the prev_unfixed key first, then assert the remainder contains no "null".

evidence.note: PrevUnfixed *int `json:"prev_unfixed"` -- no omitempty, so a nil pointer always emits null.

findings.note: Dead fixture in TestFoldFixBaseline: the mk closure declared at the top of the function is never called, and the compiler error is suppressed with a bare `_ = mk` at the end of the function. It builds a run whose init has no ParentRunID yet stamps an Origin on the transition, which would fail provenance -- i.e. it is leftover scaffolding for a case the test no longer exercises. Delete the closure and the `_ = mk` line, or restore the case it was meant to cover.

evidence.note: `_ = mk` suppressing an unused-variable error for a fixture the test never invokes.

findings.note: TestFoldRefusesANodeOutputWithNoOutput asserts only that Fold returns a non-nil error, not that the error is a *FoldError with Reason bad_payload. Every other negative case in this file goes through expectReason, which pins {Code, Reason, Seq, Type}. Because the test mutates evs[last].Data in place without re-chaining, a future change that (for example) started verifying Prev in Apply would make this test pass for an entirely unrelated reason while the regression it documents in its own 8-line comment went unguarded. Use expectReason(t, evs, ReasonBadPayload, int64(len(evs)), TypeNodeOutput).

evidence.note: t.Fatal("a node_output whose payload omits output was accepted") guarded only by `if _, err := Fold(evs); err == nil`.

findings.note: Spec section 8 row R2 requires one row per Reason asserting {Code, Reason, Seq, Type}. Three reasons are asserted on Reason alone: oversize (TestFoldCaps and TestFoldCapsPerField compare only fe.Reason), tokens_negative and tokens_too_large (TestFoldTokensNegativeAndNextIndex compares only err.(*FoldError).Reason). A wrong Code mapping in errors.go CodeFor for these three would not be caught by this package. Note the type assertions there are also unchecked (err.(*FoldError).Reason), which turns a wrong error type into a panic rather than a test failure; they are safe today only because Fold provably returns *FoldError.

evidence.note: oversize at-cap/over-cap rows compare fe.Reason only, never fe.Code, fe.Seq or fe.Type.
tokens_negative and tokens_too_large rows use err.(*FoldError).Reason without an ok check and without Code/Seq/Type.

findings.note: Spec section 8 row R4 calls for a mutation table of {delete, duplicate, swap} across 16 event types with enumerated outcomes. TestFoldPrefixesAndMutations delivers the delete class across every index of the happy log (all collapsing to the single outcome seq_gap), plus exactly one re-chained delete, two duplicates and one swap. The per-type enumeration the spec asks for is not present, so type-specific mutation outcomes -- for instance duplicating a delta_applied (second_delta) or swapping a node_output with its delta (delta_without_output) -- rest on other tests rather than on this table. Statement coverage is 100%, so this is a thoroughness gap against the stated test contract rather than an uncovered code path.
